title: Supervising V between turns
summary: supervisor.set arms an entry for V with a goal (hold_position, idle_safe), invariants (not_in_combat, no_contact, not_on_road, alive) and fixed policy actions, evaluated on the game tick at 3 Hz; it yields at once to the player's own input and keeps a receipt of every intervention.

rows.note: A hostile civilian stand-in never started a fight; the combat fixture came in 0.8.18.
A violation 0.1 s after a teleport, then player.stop and a teleport back 0.6 s later.
Yielded on mapped W (Borg 2) and on a raw mouse axis (Borg 3).
Aim, fire and reload need a weapon fixture.
Armed, then game_load: ended world_detach, nothing left.

limits: Explicit autonomous candidate only; unknown road and partial contact coverage stay explicit in every receipt.
quirks: Kill, pause, handover, load, disconnect and replacement invalidate queued work.

title: Supervising XF actors
summary: Up to five actor-keyed entries: an XF actor takes hold_position or idle_safe, alive, not_in_combat or not_lost, and release, return_last_safe, handover or pause_world.
limits: Five entries at most (supervisor_limit); an actor's entry needs the NPC write class, not the player class. Picked passers-by and spawned objects still refuse.

title: While you were away
summary: game.catchup's supervisor_summary reconciles every violation and action with its result into a 'while you were away' line, carrying run totals and the latest receipts in the cursor.
priority_reason: Borg 4 found a reporting gap in the summary; the fix (2949a677) needs SV8155 in the next session.

known_issues.summary: The summary under-reported receipts already reported by an earlier call. 0.8.22 (2949a677) counts them and links the supervisor's own writes to its actions by cid: a reporting gap, not lost receipts.

Review of 0.8.22 (Medium): a supervisor write and its action read by different catch-up calls were never paired. Fixed in 2ff42305: unpaired writes and action cids wait in the cursor (16 each) and are counted once, in either order. Unverified in game.

notes: Borg 2 read 'while you were away: … violations 1, actions 2' after SV8152.

title: Plans
summary: A plain-data, serialisable plan: steps with a precondition, an action, anticipated outcomes, branches, bounded retries, alternatives, a fallback and a deadline, roles and a shared blackboard, the failure ladder, and one report stream ending in exactly one closing report.
priority_reason: The Story Engine's scene execution sits on it, and the batch runner (the next session's ST batch) is its first consumer.

demand.note: The engine decides what is true and what happens next; the plan decides how bodies carry it out, performs, observes and reports, and never changes the record.
Anticipated outcomes map onto the scene's declared branches; an unanticipated outcome is reported as such and takes the fallback.
A scene is a unit with a cast: joint beats, roles bound to actors, one blackboard per scene, one report stream per scene, up to 5 actors.
The ladder: retry, alternative, drop a rung, dissolve, release; the truth once, no contradiction, a safe world, closed bookkeeping.
A load cancels every plan with one signal; start a scene at phase X at time t, not resume mid-plan; reports keyed by scene, plan and step so a duplicate counts once.
The sequencer and frame-rate behaviours for staging beats (waits, conditions, per-step checks, undo).
Rows with verdicts are plans: schema-3 session scripts run on the plan module.

unknowns.question: Does the shape cover the start-at-phase entry point and idempotent reports keyed by scene, plan and step that the Story Engine asks for?
unknowns.settle_by: Review against the scene execution section with XF · Story Engine

notes: Built with fake-clock tests and the Story Engine's scene A (the pickpocketing) on stub primitives. Executed host-side only today.

title: Plans executed in the game
summary: Run plans inside the game at frame rate, so the reflexes a scene needs (avoidance, facing, holding a bark its reading time, stopping when V blocks, aborting on combat, keeping inside the area) happen without the host, with beat-level reports within about a second.

demand.note: Frame-rate reflexes in game; a report within about a second of the signal; a reflex may change how something looks, never what happened.

notes: The plan module is written as data so later in-game code can execute it; the supervisor's actor policies are its other planned consumer.

title: Scene primitives
summary: The hand-written primitives plans are made of, parameterised by roles, places and timings with no story knowledge: approach and talk, a pickpocket's pass, paying at a stall, a shove, fleeing, following, waiting with an idle, leaving the area.

demand.note: The bridge owns the primitives and the executor; the engine owns composition. Fixtures: the market pickpocketing, the Friday collection, a warning under D-30.

notes: Scene A runs on stub primitives in the plan module's tests.
